author: ojiudezue
title: v4.5.10 — HVAC runtime tunables, form-only thresholds, label renames
summary: Tier 2 cycle that promotes 7 hardcoded HVAC behavior values to runtime Number entities, adds 5 form-only thresholds for set-and-forget tuning, adds a master switch for the entire solar-gain cover management feature, and renames two opaque entity labels ('Zone Intelligence' → 'Per-Zone HVAC Control'; 'Zone Sweep' → 'Vacancy Auto-Off') without touching CONF/entity_id. Closes the audit started after v4.5.9.x where user observed that climate-specific behavior values were hardcoded module constants with no UI surface. Defaults preserve v4.5.9.x behavior exactly.

decisions.decision: Single factory function `_hvac_tunable_number_factory` produces all 7 v4.5.10 Number entity classes
alternatives_considered: Hand-write 7 individual NumberEntity subclasses (~70 LoC each = ~500 LoC of boilerplate)
Single generic `HVACTunableNumber` class with constructor params (loses static class identity for HA entity registry)
Mix: factory for the 4 cover-related, hand-written for the 3 fan/predictor (asymmetric)
decisions.why: All 7 entities share the same shape: live on the HVAC Coordinator device, read form-seed from CM entry, RestoreEntity-backed slider, push to a sub-controller's runtime field via setattr, deferred-push on cross-coord init race. Factory deduplicates ~350 LoC of boilerplate to ~150 LoC of factory + ~70 LoC of 7 invocations. Each invocation is essentially a config dict — easy to add #8 / #9 in v4.5.11. Modeled on `_ec_switch_factory` from switch.py (5 EC switches via the same pattern).
decisions.implications: Future Number entities for HVAC tunables can be added by appending one factory call to `_build_hvac_v4510_numbers()`. The factory enforces consistent behavior (mirror pattern, RestoreEntity, deferred-push race handling) — bugs in one entity become bugs in all 7 (good for finding/fixing; bad if the bug is subtle). v4.5.10 review verified the factory's `_push_to_controller` semantics across all 7 instantiations.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If a future v4.5.x or v4.6.x adds an HVAC tunable that doesn't fit the pattern (e.g. needs a Select instead of a Number, or pushes to multiple sub-controllers), break it into a separate hand-written class rather than bloating the factory.

decisions.decision: Rename two switch entities by `_attr_name` only — keep CONF, entity_id, unique_id unchanged
alternatives_considered: Full rename including CONF + entity_id + migration helper (per the plan's 'three-tier rename' analysis)
Leave names as-is and rely on helper text (loses UI clarity)
decisions.why: User explicitly stated: 'I do not think we should rename constants, just labels.' The CONF + entity_id rename costs are real: dashboard tile breakage, automation YAML breakage, template breakage. The benefit (semantic alignment in code) is small for a single-user system. The label-only rename gives 100% of the UI clarity benefit at 0% of the dashboard-breakage cost. Mirror pattern: friendly_name is the user-facing surface; entity_id is the API surface. They serve different audiences.
decisions.implications: Going forward, any rename request defaults to label-only unless there's a structural reason to touch the CONF (e.g. field is being deleted, or being moved to a different scope). Documents 'label vs CONF rename' as a explicit decision the team makes per case. Source-contract tests assert unique_id is unchanged so a future contributor can't accidentally rename it.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If URA ever distributes to additional users (HACS, family installs), the per-user dashboard cost of an entity_id change becomes higher; if anything we'd lock down rename-the-CONF even harder.

decisions.decision: Master switch (`Solar Cover Management`) added as the third gating layer for solar-gain cover management
alternatives_considered: Rely on per-room `CONF_COVER_HVAC_MANAGED` opt-out (clunky — 28 rooms to flip individually)
Hide entire feature behind a global flag with no UI (no escape hatch for emergencies)
decisions.why: User's question 'is there a global toggle to turn it all off?' surfaced a real gap. Symmetric to existing `CONF_HVAC_FAN_CONTROL_ENABLED` for fans (added v4.0.15). Three-layer gating model now: (1) master switch (house-wide), (2) per-room `cover_hvac_managed` (room-wide), (3) per-decision intent + occupancy gates (cover-by-cover). Master switch is the emergency-stop / experiment-pause; per-room is for set-and-forget exclusions; per-decision is the normal logic. The October v4.5.0.4 incident (venetian blinds raised at 18:00) would have been less stressful if the user could flip the master OFF while the fix shipped.
decisions.implications: Adds a new code path (early-return in `CoverController.update`) that must stay first — verified by source-contract test asserting the check appears textually before `_get_outdoor_temp`. The switch's state survives restart via RestoreEntity. New v4.5.x cycles that add cover-related logic should respect the master.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If a future analytics/observability feature wants to track 'time HVAC cover management was disabled,' add a metric off this switch's transitions.

decisions.decision: Form-save validation rejects Cover Open Temp ≥ Cover Close Temp − 3°F with a localized error string
alternatives_considered: Runtime-only check with log warning (silent acceptance at form-save time; users wonder why it doesn't behave as set)
Coerce the user's value (auto-adjust open to close − 3°F) without warning
Skip validation entirely (lets users set whatever)
decisions.why: v4.5.10's solar-gain logic flaps if hysteresis < 3°F (verified in v3.8.4 README — 5°F was original; 3°F is the relaxed minimum). Catching at form-save means the user sees their mistake immediately with a message that explains why, not 6 hours later when they notice covers cycling. Voluptuous would also work but the manual check inside the step handler is simpler for a single rule and matches existing URA patterns. Constant `COVER_HYSTERESIS_MIN_GAP = 3.0` is the source of truth used in both validator and helper text — drift-proof.
decisions.implications: Establishes a pattern for paired-form-field validation in URA. Future paired tunables (e.g. pre-cool start hour vs end hour) should follow the same shape: shared constant + check inside step handler + localized error string in `errors` block in strings.json. Source-contract test asserts the validator block exists.
decisions.revisit_trigger: If users find the 3°F gap arbitrary in their climate (e.g. very stable outdoor temps benefit from tighter hysteresis), make `COVER_HYSTERESIS_MIN_GAP` itself configurable. Until then, hardcoded constant.

refs.what_prompted_this: User audit conversation on 2026-05-10 about which HVAC behavior values deserved UI controls. Three threads: (1) OCCUPIED_CLOSE_TEMP_DELTA hardcoded vs configurable (gap from v4.5.9.2); (2) request for full audit of HC tunables with DO/DON'T columns and short Device-UI labels; (3) request for label refinements + better names for opaque switches (Zone Intelligence + Zone Sweep). Bundled into a single Tier 2 cycle for review/test efficiency.
